oneLiner: 资源有限，而人的欲望几乎无限，所以必须做选择。
oneLinerEn: Resources are limited while wants are not, so choices must be made.
detail: 稀缺是经济学的起点。它不是说「东西很少」，而是说相对于所有人的欲望，任何资源都不够分。时间、注意力、土地、清洁空气都稀缺，因此每一份资源用在某处，就意味着别处得不到。经济学研究的正是「在稀缺条件下如何分配」。
detailEn: Scarcity is where economics begins. It does not mean goods are rare; it means that relative to all human wants, no resource is ever enough. Time, attention, land and clean air are all scarce, so using a resource one way means it cannot be used another way. Economics studies how allocation happens under scarcity.
example: 一个月工资只有一万元：交房租就不能全存下来，买电脑就少一次旅行。钱是稀缺的，所以要排序。
exampleEn: A monthly salary of 10,000: paying rent means less saving, buying a laptop means one less trip. Money is scarce, so priorities are needed.

oneLiner: 要得到一样东西，往往必须放弃另一样东西。
oneLinerEn: To get one thing, you usually have to give up another.
detail: 因为稀缺，任何选择都是取舍。个人在「工作与闲暇」之间取舍，企业在「成本与质量」之间取舍，政府在「效率与公平」之间取舍。承认取舍，是避免「什么都想要」式空谈的第一道门槛。
detailEn: Because of scarcity, every choice is a trade-off: individuals trade work against leisure, firms trade cost against quality, governments trade efficiency against equity. Acknowledging trade-offs is the first defence against promises that everything can be had at once.
example: 一门选修课选了经济学，就少了同一时段的摄影课；多睡一小时，就少一小时复习。
exampleEn: Choosing an economics elective means missing the photography class in the same slot; one more hour of sleep is one hour less of revision.

oneLiner: 为了得到某样东西而放弃的最有价值的其他选择。
oneLinerEn: The value of the best alternative you give up.
detail: 机会成本不等于花掉的钱，而等于「被放弃的最好选项」。它可以包含时间、精力、情绪甚至未来的可能性。做决策时真正该比较的，是「做这件事」相对「做另一件最好的事」的差额，而不是只看账面支出。
detailEn: Opportunity cost is not the money spent but the best forgone alternative — including time, effort, mood and future options. Good decisions compare doing this against doing the best alternative, not merely against the cash outlay.
example: 用一小时打游戏的成本，可能是这一小时本可以赚到的钱、学到的东西或休息恢复的精力。
exampleEn: The cost of an hour of gaming is the money, learning or rest that hour could have produced.

oneLiner: 决策看的是「多做一单位」带来的额外收益与成本。
oneLinerEn: Decisions hinge on the extra benefit and cost of one more unit.
detail: 理性选择很少是「要不要做这件事」，而是「还要不要再多做一点」。只要多一单位的边际收益大于边际成本，就应该继续；反之则停。边际分析解释了为什么「平均成本很低」也可能不值得扩张。
detailEn: Rational choice is rarely all-or-nothing: it asks whether to do one more unit. Keep going while marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost, and stop when it does not. This is why a low average cost does not automatically justify expanding.
example: 自助餐已经吃回本了，是否再拿一份取决于「多一口的满足」是否大于「撑得难受」的代价。
exampleEn: At a buffet you have already got your money's worth; whether to take one more plate depends on whether the extra bite beats the discomfort.

oneLiner: 人们会对奖励与惩罚作出反应，规则一变，行为就变。
oneLinerEn: People respond to rewards and penalties; change the rules and behaviour changes.
detail: 激励是经济学最有解释力的工具之一。政策、价格、税收、罚款、KPI 都是激励设计。关键难点在于：激励往往带来意料之外的应对方式（如按代码行数考核就会写出更多冗余代码）。
detailEn: Incentives are among the most powerful explanatory tools in economics: prices, taxes, fines and KPIs are all incentive designs. The hard part is unintended adaptation — paying per line of code simply produces more lines of code.
example: 超市塑料袋收费后使用量骤降；公司按加班时长算绩效，办公室就没人准时走。
exampleEn: Charging for plastic bags cuts their use; paying by hours worked keeps desks occupied after hours.

oneLiner: 已经花掉且无法收回的成本，不该影响下一步决策。
oneLinerEn: Costs already spent and unrecoverable should not drive the next decision.
detail: 理性决策只比较「从现在往后的成本与收益」。但由于厌恶浪费，人常因为「都投入这么多了」而继续投入，这就是沉没成本谬误。识别它的办法是问：如果今天从零开始，我还会选这条路吗？
detailEn: Rational decisions compare only future costs and benefits. Because waste feels bad, people keep investing because of what is already spent — the sunk-cost fallacy. The test: if I started from zero today, would I still choose this path?
example: 电影很难看，但「票都买了」让人硬撑两小时——票钱是沉没成本，时间不是。
exampleEn: A bad film plus a bought ticket keeps people seated for two hours: the ticket is sunk, the time is not.

oneLiner: 价格越高，愿意卖的人越多、想买的人越少。
oneLinerEn: Higher prices bring more sellers and fewer buyers.
detail: 需求曲线向下倾斜：价格越低，买得越多。供给曲线向上倾斜：价格越高，卖得越多。两条曲线相交决定成交价格与数量。几乎所有价格现象——从房租到机票到菜价——都可以先用供需框架拆一遍。
detailEn: Demand slopes down: the cheaper it is, the more is bought. Supply slopes up: the higher the price, the more is offered. Their intersection sets price and quantity, making supply and demand the first lens for nearly any price puzzle, from rent to airfare to vegetables.
example: 节前机票贵，是因为同期出行需求暴增而座位数量基本固定。
exampleEn: Holiday airfares jump because travel demand spikes while seats are fixed.

oneLiner: 供给量正好等于需求量时的那个价格。
oneLinerEn: The price at which quantity supplied equals quantity demanded.
detail: 价格高于均衡点会积压库存，卖方降价；低于均衡点会排队抢购，买方加价。这种自发调整就是「看不见的手」的日常版本。现实市场会有摩擦（信息、管制、垄断），因此均衡常是方向而非精确落点。
detailEn: Above equilibrium, unsold stock forces sellers to cut prices; below it, queues let buyers bid up. This self-correction is the everyday version of the invisible hand. Real markets have frictions — information, regulation, monopoly — so equilibrium is a direction, not an exact landing point.
example: 二手平台上同一款手机标价过高没人问，卖家自然会降价直到有人接手。
exampleEn: An overpriced phone on a second-hand platform attracts no messages until the seller cuts the price.

oneLiner: 价格变一点，需求量变多少——变得多就是有弹性。
oneLinerEn: How much quantity responds to a price change: a big response means elastic.
detail: 弹性衡量的是「敏感度」。替代品多、非必需、占支出比例大的商品通常更有弹性（如某品牌饮料）；替代品少、必需的商品则缺乏弹性（如胰岛素、汽油短期需求）。弹性直接决定涨价能否增加收入。
detailEn: Elasticity measures sensitivity. Goods with many substitutes, that are discretionary or take a large share of spending tend to be elastic; goods with few substitutes and inelastic demand — insulin, petrol in the short run — are not. Elasticity decides whether a price rise actually raises revenue.
example: 地铁票涨价后乘客基本不变（缺乏弹性），而某款奶茶涨价后销量暴跌（富有弹性）。
exampleEn: Raising metro fares barely changes ridership (inelastic), while a milk-tea brand raising prices can lose most of its sales (elastic).

oneLiner: 价格被压在均衡之外，就会出现卖不掉或买不到。
oneLinerEn: Hold price away from equilibrium and you get either unsold stock or queues.
detail: 价格高于均衡 → 供大于求（过剩）；价格低于均衡 → 供不应求（短缺）。价格管制、补贴、限价都可能制造这两种结果，而市场会用其他方式补偿：排队、黄牛、配给、走后门、质量下降。
detailEn: Price above equilibrium creates surplus; below it creates shortage. Price controls, subsidies and caps can generate either, and markets compensate in other ways: queues, scalpers, rationing, favours, or lower quality.
example: 票价限价后出现黄牛；房租管制长期实行后，房东减少维护、房源供给萎缩。
exampleEn: Ticket price caps breed scalpers; long-standing rent controls reduce maintenance and shrink the rental stock.

sources.label: 弗里德曼《资本主义与自由》

oneLiner: 你的行为影响了第三方，但没有为此付费或得到补偿。
oneLinerEn: Your action affects a third party without payment or compensation.
detail: 负外部性（污染、噪音、拥堵）让社会成本高于私人成本，市场会生产过多；正外部性（疫苗、教育、研发）让社会收益高于私人收益，市场会生产过少。对策通常是征税、补贴、产权界定或直接管制。
detailEn: Negative externalities (pollution, noise, congestion) make social cost exceed private cost, so markets overproduce; positive ones (vaccines, education, R&D) make social benefit exceed private benefit, so markets underproduce. Common remedies: taxes, subsidies, property rights, regulation.
example: 工厂排污自己省了钱，下游居民承担健康成本；这就是需要环保税或排放权交易的原因。
exampleEn: A factory saves money by dumping waste while downstream residents bear the health cost — the case for pollution taxes or permit trading.

oneLiner: 所有人都能用、且很难阻止别人搭便车的物品。
oneLinerEn: Goods everyone can use and no one can easily be excluded from.
detail: 公共品具备「非排他性」与「非竞争性」：国防、路灯、基础研究、公共广播。因为无法阻止搭便车，私人不愿提供，通常由政府或集体行动供给。难点在于「愿意付多少」难以显示真实偏好。
detailEn: Public goods are non-excludable and non-rival: national defence, street lights, basic research, public broadcasting. Since free-riding cannot be stopped, private provision is scarce and governments or collective action step in. The hard part is eliciting true willingness to pay.
example: 小区里没人愿意独自出钱装公共监控，但装上后所有住户都受益。
exampleEn: No single resident will fund CCTV alone, yet once installed every household benefits.

sources.label: 萨缪尔森《公共支出的纯理论》
sources.labelEn: Samuelson, The Pure Theory of Public Expenditure

oneLiner: 从完全竞争到垄断，卖家的数量决定了定价权。
oneLinerEn: From perfect competition to monopoly, the number of sellers sets pricing power.
detail: 完全竞争（众多小卖家、同质产品）中企业只能是价格接受者；垄断（唯一卖家）可以定价但受需求约束；现实中更多是垄断竞争与寡头（品牌差异化、少数几家博弈）。集中度、进入壁垒、产品差异是关键变量。
detailEn: In perfect competition many small sellers of identical goods are price takers; a monopolist sets price but is limited by demand. Reality is mostly monopolistic competition and oligopoly — differentiation plus a few players. Concentration, entry barriers and differentiation are the key variables.
example: 街边小吃摊几乎没有定价权，而手机操作系统市场长期只有两家主要玩家。
exampleEn: Street food stalls have almost no pricing power, while mobile operating systems have long had only two main players.

sources.label: 泰勒尔《产业组织理论》
sources.labelEn: Tirole, The Theory of Industrial Organization

oneLiner: 就算你样样不如人，专注于相对成本最低的事，双方仍能获益。
oneLinerEn: Even if you are worse at everything, specialising where your relative cost is lowest benefits both sides.
detail: 比较优势看的是「机会成本」而非绝对效率。李嘉图指出：只要两国生产两种商品的相对成本不同，专业化分工并交换就能扩大总产出。这是支持贸易互利最核心、也最容易被误读的论证。
detailEn: Comparative advantage compares opportunity costs, not absolute productivity. Ricardo showed that whenever two countries face different relative costs, specialisation plus exchange raises total output — the core argument for mutual gains from trade, and the most misread one.
example: 律师打字也比助理快，但律师每打一小时字就少赚一小时咨询费，于是让助理打字对双方都更好。
exampleEn: A lawyer may type faster than an assistant, but every hour typing costs an hour of billable advice — delegating makes both better off.

sources.label: 李嘉图《政治经济学及赋税原理》
sources.labelEn: Ricardo, On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation

oneLiner: 一个国家在一年内新生产出的最终商品与服务总价值。
oneLinerEn: The total value of final goods and services produced within a country in a year.
detail: GDP 有三种等价算法：生产法、收入法、支出法（C+I+G+NX）。它是「流量」而非「存量」，衡量的是产出而非财富或幸福感。人均 GDP 常被用作发展水平近似指标，但它遗漏家务劳动、环境损耗与分配状况。
detailEn: GDP can be computed three equivalent ways: production, income, or expenditure (C+I+G+NX). It is a flow, not a stock — output, not wealth or wellbeing. GDP per capita is a rough proxy for development that ignores unpaid work, environmental damage and distribution.
example: 自己做饭不计入 GDP，同一个人去餐厅吃饭就计入——因为后者发生了市场交易。
exampleEn: Cooking at home is not counted in GDP; buying the same meal at a restaurant is, because a market transaction occurs.

sources.label: 联合国 SNA 2008 国民账户体系

oneLiner: 整体物价水平持续上涨，钱的购买力持续下降。
oneLinerEn: A sustained rise in the general price level, eroding the value of money.
detail: 温和通胀（多数央行目标约 2%）通常伴随经济增长；恶性通胀则摧毁货币信用。主要成因包括需求拉动、成本推动与货币因素。通胀对存款人、固定收入者不利，对债务人有利，因此也是一种财富再分配。
detailEn: Moderate inflation (many central banks target around 2%) usually accompanies growth; hyperinflation destroys a currency's credibility. Common drivers are demand-pull, cost-push and monetary factors. Inflation hurts savers and fixed-income earners and helps borrowers — it redistributes wealth.
example: 十年前 10 元能吃一顿午饭，现在可能只够一杯饮料：不是饭变贵了，而是钱变薄了。
exampleEn: Ten yuan once bought lunch and now buys a drink: the meal did not get fancier, the money got thinner.

sources.label: IMF《世界经济展望》通胀数据说明
sources.labelEn: IMF World Economic Outlook, data notes

oneLiner: 有劳动能力、愿意工作却找不到工作的人所占的比例。
oneLinerEn: The share of people able and willing to work who cannot find a job.
detail: 失业分摩擦性（换工作间隙）、结构性（技能与岗位错配）、周期性（需求不足）。统计口径很关键：放弃找工作的人不计入失业率，因此失业率下降不总等于就业变好。奥肯法则描述了失业与产出的经验关系。
detailEn: Unemployment is frictional (between jobs), structural (skills mismatch) or cyclical (weak demand). Definitions matter: people who stop looking are excluded, so a falling rate is not always good news. Okun's law links unemployment to output empirically.
example: 工厂自动化后，原本的流水线工人技能不再匹配新岗位，这属于结构性失业。
exampleEn: When a plant automates, former assembly-line workers no longer match available jobs — structural unemployment.

sources.label: ILO 就业统计口径说明

oneLiner: 人均产出的长期提高，主要来自生产率与技术进步。
oneLinerEn: A long-run rise in output per person, driven mainly by productivity and technology.
detail: 长期增长靠的不是「多干活」，而是「同样投入产出更多」。资本积累、人力资本、技术进步与制度质量是四大来源。复利效应下，几个百分点的年均增速差异，几十年后会变成生活水平的天壤之别。
detailEn: Long-run growth comes not from working more but from producing more with the same input. Capital accumulation, human capital, technology and institutional quality are the four sources. Because of compounding, a few percentage points of annual growth becomes a vastly different standard of living within decades.
example: 年均 7% 与年均 2% 的差距，30 年后是约 7.6 倍与 1.8 倍产出的差别。
exampleEn: Over 30 years, 7% annual growth multiplies output about 7.6 times versus 1.8 times at 2%.

sources.label: 索洛《对经济增长理论的一个贡献》
sources.labelEn: Solow, A Contribution to the Theory of Economic Growth

oneLiner: 被普遍接受的交易媒介、计价单位与价值储藏。
oneLinerEn: A generally accepted medium of exchange, unit of account and store of value.
detail: 货币的三大职能缺一不可：交易媒介解决物物交换的「双重巧合」难题，计价单位降低比较成本，价值储藏让收入与支出分离。现代货币多数是信用货币，其价值来自国家信用与法定地位，而非背后的黄金。
detailEn: Money performs three functions: as a medium of exchange it solves the double coincidence of wants; as a unit of account it lowers comparison costs; as a store of value it separates earning from spending. Most modern money is fiat, backed by state credibility rather than gold.
example: 没有货币时，面包师要用面包换鞋，必须刚好找到一个想要面包的鞋匠；有了货币就无需巧合。
exampleEn: Without money a baker must find a shoemaker who wants bread right now; with money no coincidence is needed.

sources.label: 米什金《货币金融学》
sources.labelEn: Mishkin, The Economics of Money, Banking and Financial Markets

oneLiner: 资金的价格，也是把未来的钱折算到今天的折扣率。
oneLinerEn: The price of funds, and the discount rate that translates future money into today's value.
detail: 名义利率 = 实际利率 + 预期通胀（费雪方程）。利率升高会抑制借贷与投资、吸引资金流入、压低资产估值；利率降低则相反。央行通过政策利率影响整个利率体系，再传导到房贷、企业融资与汇率。
detailEn: The Fisher equation splits nominal rates into real rates plus expected inflation. Higher rates discourage borrowing and investment, attract capital and compress valuations; lower rates do the reverse. Central banks move a policy rate that transmits to mortgages, corporate funding and exchange rates.
example: 房贷利率从 4% 升到 6%，同样一笔贷款月供明显增加，购房需求随之降温。
exampleEn: A mortgage rate rising from 4% to 6% noticeably raises monthly payments, cooling housing demand.

oneLiner: 发行货币、制定利率、充当最后贷款人的机构。
oneLinerEn: The institution that issues money, sets interest rates and acts as lender of last resort.
detail: 央行的核心目标通常是物价稳定，许多还兼顾就业与金融稳定。工具包括政策利率、公开市场操作、准备金要求以及量化宽松。独立性与可信度至关重要：市场相信央行会控通胀，加息才不必过猛。
detailEn: Central banks usually target price stability, with mandates that often include employment and financial stability. Tools include the policy rate, open market operations, reserve requirements and quantitative easing. Independence and credibility matter: if markets believe inflation will be controlled, less tightening is needed.
example: 危机时央行向银行体系注入流动性，防止挤兑演变成系统性崩盘。
exampleEn: In a crisis a central bank injects liquidity into the banking system so a run does not become a systemic collapse.

sources.label: 国际清算银行（BIS）央行职能概览
sources.labelEn: BIS overview of central bank functions

oneLiner: 每个人都已选定策略，且没人能通过单方面改变而变得更好。
oneLinerEn: A set of strategies where no player gains by changing alone.
detail: 纳什均衡是一种「稳定状态」，但它不保证结果最优——囚徒困境的均衡对双方都更差。它也不保证唯一，博弈可能存在多个均衡，此时「谁先行动、如何沟通、习惯如何」决定了落点。
detailEn: Nash equilibrium is a stable state, but not necessarily a good one: the prisoner's dilemma equilibrium is worse for both. Nor is it always unique — with multiple equilibria, who moves first, how players communicate and shared habits decide which one is reached.
example: 两家公司都不打价格战是均衡；但若都怀疑对方会降价，先降价也可能成为另一个均衡。
exampleEn: Two firms both holding prices is an equilibrium; if each fears the other will cut, pre-emptive cutting can be an equilibrium too.

sources.label: 纳什《n 人博弈的均衡点》
sources.labelEn: Nash, Equilibrium Points in n-Person Games

oneLiner: 同样金额，失去的痛苦大于得到的快乐。
oneLinerEn: Losing hurts more than gaining the same amount feels good.
detail: 前景理论的核心发现之一：人对损失的心理权重约为同等收益的 1.5–2.5 倍。这解释了为什么人死守亏损股票、为什么「限时优惠」有效、为什么改革常常遭遇强烈阻力——既得利益的失去被放大。
detailEn: A central finding of prospect theory: losses carry roughly 1.5–2.5 times the psychological weight of equivalent gains. This explains holding losing positions, the power of limited-time discounts, and why reforms meet fierce resistance — losses to vested interests loom larger.
example: 捡到 100 元的开心，抵不过丢掉 100 元的难受；这会让人过度回避风险。
exampleEn: Finding 100 feels lighter than losing 100 feels heavy, which pushes people towards excessive risk aversion.

sources.label: 卡尼曼、特沃斯基《前景理论》

oneLiner: 名义上向谁征税，和实际上谁承担，是两件事。
oneLinerEn: Who is taxed by law and who bears the burden in practice are different questions.
detail: 税收负担最终由买卖双方按弹性分摊：谁更缺乏弹性（更难替代），谁承担更多。向卖方征税可能导致价格上升由买方承担，向买方征税也可能压低卖方净价。因此「让企业交税」不等于「企业真的承担」。
detailEn: The burden splits according to elasticity: the less elastic side — the one that can less easily substitute — bears more. Taxing sellers can raise prices paid by buyers; taxing buyers can cut net prices received by sellers. So 'making firms pay' does not mean firms truly bear it.
example: 对房东征税，如果住房供给缺乏弹性，税负更多落在房东身上；反之可能转成更高租金。
exampleEn: Taxing landlords shifts more of the burden onto them when housing supply is inelastic; otherwise it can reappear as higher rent.

oneLiner: 人人可用却无人拥有的资源，会被过度使用直至枯竭。
oneLinerEn: Resources open to all and owned by none are overused until depleted.
detail: 当使用收益归个人、损耗成本由群体分担时，每个人的理性行为叠加成集体灾难：过度放牧、渔业枯竭、地下水超采。奥斯特罗姆的研究表明，除了私有化与国家管制，社区自治规则也能有效治理公共池塘资源。
detailEn: When benefits are private and costs are shared, individually rational use adds up to collective ruin: overgrazing, depleted fisheries, falling water tables. Ostrom showed that beyond privatisation and state control, community-designed rules can govern common-pool resources well.
example: 共享单车早期无人约束地投放与私占，最终车辆损坏率极高、企业退出。
exampleEn: Early dockless bike-sharing saw unlimited dumping and private locking, ending in extreme damage rates and market exit.

sources.label: 奥斯特罗姆《公共事物的治理之道》

oneLiner: 交易一方知道得更多，市场可能因劣质品驱逐优质品而萎缩。
oneLinerEn: When one side knows more, markets can shrink as bad products drive out good ones.
detail: 信息不对称分两类：「逆向选择」发生在成交前（买家分不清质量，只肯出平均价），「道德风险」发生在成交后（有兜底方时行为变得更冒险）。解决方式包括信号（学历、认证、保修）、筛选（免赔额、分级定价）与第三方验证（评级、质检、平台担保）。
detailEn: Two forms: adverse selection before contracting (buyers cannot judge quality and pay an average price) and moral hazard after (protection makes behaviour riskier). Remedies include signalling (credentials, certification, warranties), screening (deductibles, tiered pricing) and third-party verification (ratings, inspection, platform guarantees).
example: 二手车市场上，卖家清楚车况而买家不清楚，买家压价使好车退出，最终市场只剩次品。
exampleEn: In used cars the seller knows the condition, buyers discount, good cars exit and the market fills with lemons.
